Because the dataset includes account-directory information and full records, it likely contains stable unique identifiers such as usernames, student IDs, staff IDs, or email addresses that allow records about the same person to be linked across backup copies and with other datasets available to the provider.
assumptions: Assumes the account directory and grade records include stable identifiers rather than being fully anonymized.

title: Third-party provider receives directly identified student and staff records
description: The cloud hosting provider receives full grade records, assignments, and the account directory. This strongly indicates processing of directly identified personal data, because account directories and educational records commonly include names, usernames, email addresses, and institutional identifiers tied to individuals.
assumptions: Assumes the transferred records are not de-identified before backup/replication.

title: Backed-up educational records can serve as attributable evidence about individuals
description: Full grade records and assignment data preserved at the cloud provider can be attributed to specific students and possibly instructors, creating durable evidence of performance, submissions, and related claims that individuals may later be unable to repudiate.
assumptions: Assumes records are associated with identifiable accounts in the transferred dataset.
uncertainty_note: The flow description does not explicitly mention signatures or audit metadata, so this is grounded in attributable data content rather than stronger non-repudiation mechanisms.

title: Backup traffic to the hosting provider can reveal the existence of educational activity
description: Regular nightly transfer of full grade records, assignments, and directory data to the external hosting provider creates observable communications whose timing, size, and destination can reveal that educational records exist and that grading or assignment activity is occurring within the service.
assumptions: Assumes the provider or an observer at that destination can observe transfer timing/volume, even if payloads are protected.
uncertainty_note: This is a weaker inference because the description does not specify who can observe the communication beyond the destination provider.

title: Full-record backup transfers an excessive amount of personal data
description: The flow sends full grade records, assignments, and the entire account directory to the cloud hosting provider. Sending complete records rather than a minimized subset for backup/replication suggests processing of more personal data than may be strictly necessary for the stated purpose, increasing disclosure risk.
assumptions: Assumes not every field in the full records is required for the backup or replication objective, or that a more minimized backup design was possible.
uncertainty_note: Backup/replication can legitimately require broad data coverage, so the excessiveness depends on architecture choices not fully described.

title: Sensitive educational data is propagated to an external third party
description: The assignment and grading service propagates full educational records and account-directory data to a third-party cloud hosting provider. This expands exposure of sensitive personal data beyond the primary service boundary and creates additional disclosure risk if the external party does not strictly need all transferred content.
assumptions: Assumes the cloud provider is a distinct external party and not merely an internal infrastructure boundary.

title: Personal data is shared with a predetermined external party
description: The flow makes full student and staff records accessible to a fixed third party, the cloud hosting provider. Sharing sensitive educational data with this predetermined external entity increases exposure and may exceed what is functionally necessary depending on the hosting arrangement.
assumptions: Assumes EE5 is outside the controller's internal trust boundary, as indicated by ExternalEntity.

title: Data subjects may be unaware that full educational records are replicated to a third-party host
description: Students and staff whose grades, assignments, and directory data are included in nightly backups may not be aware that their full records are routinely transferred to an external cloud hosting provider for backup and replication.
assumptions: Assumes this third-party backup/replication practice is not clearly communicated to data subjects.
uncertainty_note: The flow description does not state whether privacy notices or other transparency mechanisms exist.

title: Data subjects may lack practical ability to erase or rectify replicated backup copies
description: Because full records are replicated nightly to a cloud hosting provider, correcting or deleting personal data may require changes across backup copies and replicated environments. This can reduce data subjects' practical ability to have inaccurate data rectified or obsolete data erased in all locations.
assumptions: Assumes backup copies are retained and not immediately synchronized for rectification/erasure operations.
uncertainty_note: The description does not specify retention, backup lifecycle controls, or restoration procedures.

title: Nightly full backup may violate data minimization expectations
description: Transferring full grade records, assignments, and the account directory to the cloud provider may process more personal data than necessary for the backup/replication purpose, creating a risk of non-compliance with data minimization requirements.
assumptions: Assumes a less data-intensive backup design or field minimization could have met the same purpose.
uncertainty_note: Whether this is truly non-compliant depends on the necessity of full-fidelity backups in the specific operational and legal context.

title: Replicated backups may create storage-limitation compliance risk
description: Nightly replication of full educational records to the cloud hosting provider can result in multiple retained copies over time. If those copies are kept longer than necessary, the flow contributes to a storage-limitation compliance risk.
assumptions: Assumes backups are retained for a period and not immediately overwritten according to a strict retention schedule.
uncertainty_note: The flow description mentions nightly backup and replication but does not specify retention duration.

title: Third-party hosting transfer may raise lawfulness and governance concerns
description: Sending full grade records, assignments, and account-directory data to an external cloud hosting provider may require a clearly established lawful basis, contractual controls, and governance appropriate for educational records. If those are inadequate, the processing may be unlawful or insufficiently governed.
assumptions: Assumes the provider is a separate external processor or recipient requiring specific legal and contractual safeguards.
uncertainty_note: The description does not state jurisdiction, contracts, or lawful basis, so this is a plausible compliance threat rather than a confirmed issue.

title: Grade records are linkable through unique student identifiers
description: The grade records database likely stores records keyed by unique student identifiers or equivalent references so the grading service can assemble views for student, parent, and teacher audiences. This enables linking multiple grade entries and related educational records to the same individual across assignments and time.
uncertainty_note: The flow description does not enumerate fields, so the presence of explicit unique identifiers is inferred from the need to build per-student views.

title: The flow processes identified student grade information
description: To build student, parent, and teacher views, the grading service reads grade records that are likely associated with named or otherwise directly identified students. This means identified personal data is processed from the database into the service.
uncertainty_note: Direct identifiers are not explicitly listed, but identified or readily identifiable records are strongly implied by the described views.

title: Grade records can serve as attributable evidence about a student's academic performance
description: Stored grade records can be attributed to a specific student and used as evidence of academic outcomes, making it difficult for the student to deny that certain grades or performance records are associated with them once processed and displayed.
uncertainty_note: This concerns attribution of the data to the student; the flow description does not indicate signatures or stronger evidentiary mechanisms.

title: Sensitive grade data is made accessible to a predetermined set of parties
description: The grading service reads grade records specifically to build views for students, parents, and teachers. This means sensitive educational data is exposed to multiple predefined recipient groups, creating a disclosure risk if all included data elements are not strictly necessary for each audience.
uncertainty_note: The threat is grounded in the stated audiences, but the exact access controls and per-audience filtering are not described.

title: Returned grade records may be more detailed than needed for each audience view
description: A single read from the grade records database to support student, parent, and teacher views may deliver fine-grained grade information to the grading service beyond what is necessary for a particular audience-specific presentation. This creates a risk of excessive granularity at the destination process.
uncertainty_note: The description does not specify whether the database query is scoped per audience or whether minimization occurs before data reaches the service.

title: Students may be unaware that their grade records are reused to generate multiple audience views
description: The grading service processes grade records from the database to create views not only for students but also for parents and teachers. Data subjects may not be fully aware of this internal reuse and disclosure pattern, especially if transparency about downstream view generation is limited.
uncertainty_note: This depends on whether the system provides clear notices; the flow description alone does not confirm transparency measures.

title: The flow may violate data minimization if the service reads more grade data than needed
description: Because one service read supports multiple audiences, there is a risk that the grading service retrieves a broader set of grade records or attributes than necessary for a specific view. If so, the processing would exceed what is needed for the immediate purpose and raise data minimization concerns.
uncertainty_note: This is a plausible compliance risk from the architecture, but the actual query scope and filtering behavior are not provided.
